title: Bundle deadlock and stale owner: stable order, all or nothing, identity-based reclaim, fairness across films
note: Synthetic. Lists the function exercised, the input and the expected outcome; authored, not run. No number here is a measurement of real rendering, latency, memory or cost.

calls.case: task X needs encode then video_render, task Y needs video_render then encode, both launched together
outer render holds a slot; its managed child asks for the same pool with RASANAI_SLOT_OWNER set; and with a forged token
slot file whose pid is alive but 7 h old with a missed heartbeat; one whose pid is gone; one whose pid start time changed
film A holds 2 slots and has an old ticket; film B has a new interactive ticket; film C a background ticket waiting 20 min
release called by a process that is not the token owner

expect: both bundles are taken in POOL_ORDER (video_render before encode), all or nothing, and released before any wait: neither can hold encode while waiting for video_render
the child is admitted as re-entrant (units 0, not counted twice) only while the outer token still owns a slot file; the forged token is queued like any other task
alive and old is NOT reclaimed in the managed path; a dead pid and a changed pid start time are
B's interactive head start puts it first, but A's penalty for the slots it holds and C's accumulated age keep anyone from starving
release removes a slot file only when the token and pid match
